prompt: # Role - You are an AI competing in a gaming arena. # Objective - Write a complete Python file that provides the next move for a game of Go on a 19x19 board. - You must define a smart policy that is able to beat other policies in the arena. - You will be disqualified if you do not return a legal move string. Therefore, you must always return a legal move string. # Required API The provided python file must implement the following API: ```python def policy(me: list[tuple[int, int]], opponent: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> tuple[int, int]: ... ``` # State Representation - You are always the player to move. - `me` is a list of (row, col) tuples containing your stones. - `opponent` is a list of (row, col) tuples containing the opponent's stones. - Rows are indexed from 1 (top) to 19 (bottom). - Columns are indexed from 1 (left) to 19 (right). # Action / Return Format - Return exactly ONE move as a tuple `(row, col)`. - Use `(0, 0)` to pass. # Constraints - You may use any standard Python imports, including numpy. - Your code is allowed 1 second of execution time on a modern 3GHz CPU. # Output Format Requirements - Output your strategy before providing the Python source code for your policy. - Output the Python source code for your policy surrounded by `...` tags. # Example Output The strategy for this policy is... ...
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a Go policy for 19x19 that works within a 1-second time constraint, focusing on legal move validation and a layered strategy: prioritizing captures and rescues, then extending threatened groups, positioning near existing stones for influence, and opening with classical corner plays.

Implementing the core helper functions... I'm generating candidate moves near existing stones on the board, then evaluating each one by scoring captures, liberties, group safety, and opponent pressure, while also rewarding moves that connect to my own stones.

Adding penalties for edge positions and filling my own eyes, then selecting the move with the highest score. I should make sure we always return a legal move or pass if none exist, and I'm considering performance since evaluating many candidates with group computations could be slow on a 19x19 board.
